findings.notes: Gate run for the record on the single Hunter candidate. Referee verdict was NOT_A_BUG before the gate; the gate independently kills the finding at Q1. Q3/Q5/Q7 assessed for completeness; Q2 moot once Q1 fails.

Q1.detail: No attacker-use chain right now. Every path to the unguarded self-call requires the owner's own key (K1, only in-repo validator, owner ECDSA only) or an owner-installed fully-trusted executor, or the 7702 EOA key itself. No limited-scope principal exists in-repo that could reach it, and session modules live outside this repo (untraced, not assumed).

Q2.detail: Privilege-escalation impact would be on the accepted list in principle, but Q1 already fails; no impact is attainable.

Q3.detail: Root cause (if it were a bug) sits in Nexus.sol on main branch, in-scope asset.

Q4.detail: Requires privileged access (owner key / trusted executor) the attacker cannot realistically get; the 'attacker' and the privileged principal are the same party.

Q5.detail: Referee checked EX-116, EX-049, EX-I20, EX-067, EX-073/EX-074: no root-cause duplicate. #303 (unknown private report) is unretireable residual risk.

Q6.detail: No impact demonstrated beyond 'technically possible': the same principal can already run unrestricted delegatecall via execute(), install arbitrary modules, and upgrade — re-init adds nothing.

Q7.detail: Not on the never-submit list; killed on Q1/Q4 merits, not class.
